notes: The leaderboard shows each player's Steam profile picture, including pictures Steam serves from its current picture network.
A site update no longer prints a long list of peer-dependency warnings while installing the frontend.
A site update compiles MagicCore before it is published, and the site will not serve a DLL the game cannot load.
An update starts the site and the API when they are not already running.
A logo address shows in the navbar and the admin sidebar, and saving a color keeps that color on the preview.
The Site Editor is easier to use, and Detailed still reaches every color and control.
Admin includes an API reference for this site.
Updating the site finishes building the pages again, so the version you see is the version that is running.
The leaderboard loads instead of crashing while the table is opening.
The admin sidebar sits beside the page instead of covering it.
added: Admin has an API Reference for this site, and you can download the OpenAPI document.
Site Editor Simple mode changes one color, and the related colors follow it.
System Control has a Harmony mod page with the version, what changed, and a download.
A game server on the new mod checks for updates and installs them, or you can run rusttemplate.update in the server console.
The mod tells the site whether that server is Oxide or Carbon, and the server card remembers it.
Panels can be Pterodactyl, Pelican, or Calagopus. Linking a server, the console, power, and startup still work the same way.
Server tags are managed from a Tags button, and servers can be shown by tag instead of category.
User search finds a Steam ID even when that person has never signed in, and you can add them to the site.
The cookie banner text can be edited, including the footer Cookies link.
Linked kits can be filled in by hand or pulled from the game server.
Admin shows a warning when the PayNow key is missing or cannot run the store.
changed: Leaderboard names use the Steam profile picture. The first letter of the name stays when Steam has no picture.
A site update restarts the frontend onto the build it just installed.
The frontend uses ESLint 9 and TypeScript 6.0, which the Next.js lint plugins accept, so an update does not warn about those packages.
Publishing builds MagicCore.dll and checks that Rust can read it. The download skips a file that is not a real mod.
A site update starts the frontend on port 3000 and the backend on port 8000 when nothing is listening.
The navbar and the admin sidebar use the logo address you save. A large file stays in the logo box.
Saving a color in the Site Editor reloads the preview, so the color you saved stays on screen.
Editing the theme no longer resizes the rest of the page.
Site Editor Detailed lists every control. Clicking a labeled part of the preview opens that field.
A demo leaderboard fills Time played on every tab.
A site update no longer stops while installing the frontend, which had left the new version number on the old pages.
The leaderboard no longer crashes while it loads the server and wipe lists.
The admin sidebar sits beside the main section.
Chart and account menu widths follow their layout again.
Frontend and Laravel packages are on their current releases, including the editor, charts, tables, and styles.
This update needs PHP 8.3.
Opening Edit on a server and saving no longer replaces the name and address with the panel server, or turns an enabled server off.
The same RustMaps map can be used in several votes. If a map link cannot be loaded, you get an error and that vote is left as it was.
The vote page shows your site name above the server.
A logo stored on the site CDN shows in the header.
Uploads larger than 1 MB, such as a 1.5 MB logo, are accepted. New installs allow uploads up to 32 MB.
Servers with enabled turned off no longer appear on the public servers page.
Store cards decode symbols such as a middle dot, and they no longer repeat the product name.
Terms and Privacy use the date written in the page, instead of a fixed 05 August 2026.
robots.txt and the sitemap use your own site.
The footer shows your site name as soon as the page loads.
Leaderboard weapon icons load, and Time played is filled in on every tab.
Redirects such as /store to /store/ranks work even when that page already exists.
Map votes, the leaderboard, and store categories respond instead of saying they are not migrated yet.
The panel type menu shows a logo for Pterodactyl, Pelican, and Calagopus.
Sites that already updated were showing the new version while still serving the previous pages. Run update once more to load the new pages, including the Harmony mod page.
Long server names on the leaderboard stay inside the box. The box grows a little, then the name is cut off.
Tag pictures on server cards are larger.
The Cookies link in the footer lines up with Terms and Privacy.
Server lists can be aligned left, center, or right.
Theme colors such as card text now show up on the site.
Menus inside popups stay on top, so you can pick a panel, tag, or category.
Bans have their own permission for viewing, creating, removing, and syncing bans.
removed: The Rustalyzer widget is no longer on the site.
